Figure 3:Qualitative novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K and CO3Dv2.Each row shows one scene or object. From left to right, the columns contain two input
views, predictions from LVSM, PRoPE, RayRoPE, and HRoPE, and the
ground-truth target view (GT).

Figure 5:Predicted local planes on RealEstate10K.Two scenes are shown side by side; within each scene, the two rows correspond to the reference views. For each view, the columns show the input image, predicted
plane orientations overlaid on the image (Visual Plane), and per-patch normals
encoded as a color map (Normal Map). The red boxes mark the same approximately
planar surface across views, where the predicted orientations remain locally
coherent and cross-view consistent.

Figure 8:Additional qualitative comparison on RealEstate10K.Each row is one scene. From left to right, the columns show novel views synthesized
by LVSM, PRoPE, RayRoPE, and HRoPE (Ours), followed by the ground-truth target
view (GT). All methods use the same backbone and inputs and differ only in their
positional encoding.

Figure 9:Additional qualitative comparison on CO3Dv2.Each row is one object. From left to right, the columns show novel views synthesized
by LVSM, PRoPE, RayRoPE, and HRoPE (Ours), followed by the ground-truth target
view (GT). All methods use the same backbone and inputs and differ only in their
positional encoding.

Figure 10:Additional qualitative comparison with EscherNet on Objaverse.Each row is one object. From left to right, the columns show three input views, the
novel views synthesized with CaPE and HRoPE (Ours), and the ground-truth target
view (GT). Both methods use the same EscherNet backbone and inputs and differ only
